premiumNotAvailable: This feature is not available in this build.
deleteContactConfirmMsg: Are you sure you want to delete this contact? You will lose all chats and will no longer be able to decrypt their messages or encrypt messages for them.
unknownSender: Unknown sender contact. Import it first.
deleteMessageConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this message?
localOnlyVersion: In this version, all keys and messages are stored only on this device.
onboardingSubtitle: Create a new identity or restore an existing one.
scanIdentityQrHint: Scan a Layergram identity QR code
wordMismatch: The selected word does not match.
appLockSubtitle: Require PIN or biometrics to open Layergram
noPinSet: No PIN configured. Set a PIN in settings.
privacyShield: Privacy shield active while app is in background.
resetIdentitySubtitle: Deletes local identity, contacts and history. The app will restart as freshly installed.
confirmResetBody1: This operation will delete the local identity, all contacts and all chats. This cannot be undone.
confirmResetBody2: If you have not written down your recovery phrase, you will lose the ability to restore this identity. After reset,
confirmResetBody3: some messages already received may no longer be decryptable because local Forward Secrecy session state is deleted.
confirmResetFinalBody1: This action will permanently delete identity, contacts and chats.
confirmResetFinalBody2: Your recovery phrase restores the identity, not the local Forward Secrecy session state.
confirmResetFinalBody3: After reset, some messages already received may no longer be decryptable. Are you absolutely sure you want to proceed?
dataClearedSnackbar: Data deleted. Restart or create a new identity.
displayNameLabel: Display name in the sharable identity
shareQrHint: Share this QR: your contacts can scan it from Layergram.
shareLinkHeading: Share your contact via this link. The person receiving it can click or paste it in Layergram and you will be added to their contacts.
recoveryPhraseWarning1: Keep the paper copy of your recovery phrase in a safe place. Do not store it in a screenshot, notes app, file, or cloud drive.
recoveryPhraseWarning2: If you lose it and lose your device, you will no longer be able to decrypt received messages. If someone obtains it, they could decrypt messages received on your behalf.
enterNameError: Enter the name you will appear as to contacts
recoveryPhraseSaveWarning: Write these words on paper and keep them somewhere safe: without this phrase you will never be able to decrypt received messages if you lose your device or delete the app.
pasteLinkLabel: Paste the Layergram Link of the contact you want to add
pasteLinkHint: Paste the URL copied from the contact (e.g. layergram://...).
invalidLayergramLink: Invalid Layergram link. Make sure it starts with layergram://
invalidQrCode: Invalid QR. Try with a Layergram link or a QR generated by Layergram.
contactNameHint: Use an anonymous or made-up nickname
contactNameHelper: For more privacy, choose an anonymous nickname or a made-up name.
screenProtectionSubtitle: Protect messages from screenshots and screen recording
hideChatPreviewSubtitle: Hide message previews in the chat list (still visible during search)
sessionDecryptionCacheSubtitle: Preload recent chat decryption keys in RAM only while the app is open and unlocked. No plaintext is stored, and the cache is cleared when the app is hidden, locked, the identity or passphrase changes, or the app closes.
deleteChatConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete the entire chat? This action cannot be undone.
coreLicense: Licensed under the Apache License 2.0. See LICENSE file for details.
passphraseDeactivateBody: The passphrase-derived keys will be destroyed. Messages encrypted with this passphrase will no longer be visible.
passphraseWarning: This phrase must remain secret and works in combination with the current identity. If you lose this secret phrase, or the identity recovery phrase, you will permanently lose access to the messages for this identity+passphrase pair. To learn more
onboardingLegalConsent: I have read and agree to the {terms} and {privacy}.
coverLengthLimit: Cover message length limit (including hidden characters)
wordMismatchRetry: Word mismatch. Would you like to try again?
verifyContactCeremonyIntro: Compare these codes with {name} on a voice call or in person. If both of you see the same values, the contact is authentic.
verifyContactMismatchBody: If the codes do not match, the key you imported may have been tampered with during the exchange. Do not verify this contact and consider deleting and re-importing it through a trusted channel.
verifyContactRevokedSnackbar: {name} is no longer marked as verified
chatUnverifiedBannerBody: This contact has not been verified yet. You can still exchange messages, but the authenticity of their key has not been confirmed.
onboardingIntro: Layergram uses a key pair instead of an account. Your private key stays on this device; your public identity is what contacts use to add you.
onboardingGuideHint: Need the step-by-step guide while using the app? Open it on this device and come back here when you are ready.
onboardingStepCreateBody: Choose this if this is your first time using Layergram.
onboardingStepSaveBody: Write it on paper and keep it private. It protects access to your identity.
onboardingStepShareBody: Use your QR or link so another person can add you.
onboardingStepContactBody: Import their Layergram link or scan their QR.
onboardingCreateModeTitle: First time here? Create a new identity.
onboardingCreateModeBody: This is the normal path for new users. Layergram will generate a new private key and public identity for you.
onboardingRestoreModeTitle: Restore only if you already have a recovery phrase.
onboardingRestoreModeBody: Use this when you previously created a Layergram identity and want to bring that same identity onto this device.
onboardingCreateHelper: Pick the name contacts will see when you share your public identity. You can change it later.
onboardingRestoreHelper: Enter the name contacts should see, then paste the recovery phrase from the identity you already created.
recoveryPhraseDialogBody: These words are your recovery phrase. They can restore your Layergram identity, so write them on paper before continuing.
recoveryPhraseDialogPrivacyNote: Do not store this phrase in screenshots, notes, files, or cloud drives. Contacts only need your public identity link or QR after setup.
confirmWordBody: To make sure the phrase was copied correctly, Layergram asks for one word from it.
identityCreatedBody: Next you will see My Identity. Share the QR or link from that page so someone can add you, then add their identity from the Contacts page.
identityCreatedPublicKeyNote: Sharing your public identity is safe. Never share the recovery phrase you just wrote down.
shareAndroidWhatsAppWarning: If the message appears truncated in WhatsApp, use "Copy" and paste it manually.
shareAndroidWhatsAppDialogContent: WhatsApp truncates shared text. Open WhatsApp and paste the message manually to send it completely.
shareAndroidTelegramDialogContent: Telegram filters out zero-width characters, removing Layergram hidden messages. Sharing via this app is not recommended.
security.fs.warning.recoverability: If you lose access to this device, messages protected by Forward Secrecy cannot be recovered.
security.fs.warning.device_bound: Maximum Forward Secrecy links this conversation to your current device. Switching devices will require re-establishing the session.
security.fs.warning.pending_activation: Forward Secrecy upgrade is pending. Send a message to complete the handshake.
security.fs.warning.fallback_allowed: Forward Secrecy messages are ratchet-only. Messages are not duplicated with the legacy identity key.
security.fs.warning.no_silent_downgrade: Maximum Forward Secrecy is active. Messages cannot be sent without a confirmed secure channel.
security.fs.new_device_detected: New device or session detected for this contact. A new secure session is being negotiated.
security.fs.message_lost: This message was encrypted with a previous session and cannot be decrypted.
security.fs.session_reset_done: Secure session reset. A new session will be negotiated automatically.
security.fs.error.session_broken: This secure session is broken and cannot be used.
security.fs.error.device_repair_required: Maximum Forward Secrecy requires device repair before sending.
security.fs.error.unexpected_device: Unexpected device detected. Repair the secure session before sending.
security.fs.error.sending_blocked: Maximum Forward Secrecy prevents sending in the current state.
security.fs.info.title: Security with this contact
security.fs.info.legacy_description: Messages are encrypted end-to-end. Forward Secrecy will activate automatically as you exchange messages.
security.fs.info.active_description: Forward Secrecy is active. Each message uses a unique key derived from an ephemeral handshake.
security.fs.info.active_advantage: Past messages remain protected even if your keys are later compromised.
security.fs.info.strict_description: Maximum Forward Secrecy is active and bound to this device. Messages can only be sent and received through this confirmed secure channel.
security.fs.info.broken_description: The secure channel could not be verified. No messages have been sent or received in this state.
security.fs.info.upgrading_description: Forward Secrecy is upgrading automatically. Continue exchanging messages to complete the secure session.
security.fs.maximum.confirm_body: This will bind the conversation to your current device. You will need to repeat this process if you switch devices.
security.fs.maximum.pending_notice: Waiting for {contact} to confirm Maximum Forward Secrecy.
security.fs.maximum.setup_outgoing_body: This will send only a setup message. Your message text will stay here. Take turns exchanging setup messages until Maximum FS is active, then send your message again.
security.fs.maximum.setup_incoming_body: This was only a setup message. Take turns exchanging setup messages until Maximum FS is active. No message text was sent yet.
security.fs.info.legacy_advantages: Maximum compatibility with all your devices. Works across multiple devices simultaneously. Forward Secrecy upgrades automatically when supported.
security.fs.info.legacy_keep_in_mind: These messages are not yet protected by Forward Secrecy. Upgrade happens automatically as you exchange messages.
security.fs.info.upgrading_advantages: Improves protection automatically. Keeps compatibility across all your devices.
security.fs.info.upgrading_keep_in_mind: Forward Secrecy applies only after the secure session is established. This happens automatically by exchanging messages.
security.fs.info.active_keep_in_mind: If this contact changes device or reinstalls Layergram, a new secure session may be needed.
security.fs.info.strict_advantages: Strongest protection for this contact. Prevents silent downgrade for user messages.
security.fs.info.strict_keep_in_mind: If either person changes device, reinstalls Layergram, or loses session state, sending may pause until the session is repaired. Some old messages may not be recoverable.
security.fs.info.strict_requested_descri: You requested Maximum Forward Secrecy for this contact. It is not active yet — Layergram is waiting for a confirmed secure session.
security.fs.info.strict_requested_advant: Prepares this contact for the strongest device-bound mode.
security.fs.info.strict_requested_keep_i: You and this contact should agree to use the expected device(s). Messages may not be readable from other devices until a new secure session is established.
security.fs.info.broken_keep_in_mind: Repair or re-establish the secure session before sending.
security.fs.info.suspended_description: A previous Forward Secure session cannot currently be used. Layergram may retry negotiation.
security.fs.info.suspended_keep_in_mind: Send a message to trigger a new secure session upgrade.
security.fs.progress.one_more_exchange: One more message exchange to activate
security.fs.warning.recoverability_title: Some messages may not be readable later
security.fs.warning.recoverability_body: This mode improves protection by reducing how long old keys or readable history remain available. If you delete messages, reset sessions, reinstall Layergram, or clean the encrypted archive, some older messages may not be recoverable even if you still have the correct passphrase.
security.fs.warning.recoverability_confi: I understand that some old messages may become unrecoverable.
security.fs.warning.device_bound_title: This mode is bound to verified devices
security.fs.warning.device_bound_body: Use it only if you and this contact agree to use the expected device(s). If either person changes device, reinstalls Layergram, resets sessions, or uses an older version, messages may not be readable until a new secure session is established.
security.fs.warning.device_bound_confirm: I have agreed this with the contact and understand that this mode is device-bound.
security.fs.warning.pending_body: Maximum FS is not active yet. Layergram is waiting for a confirmed secure session. Until confirmation, Layergram can send setup messages but not your message text.
security.fs.warning.fallback_body: Legacy FS fallback is disabled. If an older message contains fallback material, Layergram will not use it without a matching FS session.
security.fs.card.title: Security for this context
security.fs.card.no_sessions: No active sessions with this contact.
security.fs.card.explanation_prefix: Forward Secrecy activates automatically as you exchange messages. It protects only messages sent after the secure session is established. Messages sent before this upgrade remain protected by the previous Layergram encryption model.
security.passphrase.settings_visible_not: These settings are only available while your passphrase context is active.
security.fs.mode.sheet_subtitle: Choose the Forward Secrecy level for this contact.
security.fs.mode.advanced_desc: Automatic Forward Secrecy when supported. No legacy content fallback.
security.fs.cls.legacy.desc: This message uses standard Layergram identity encryption. Forward Secrecy was not active.
security.fs.cls.pre_fs.desc: This message was sent before Forward Secrecy was established and is not protected by FS.
security.fs.cls.negotiation.desc: This message was part of the Forward Secrecy handshake negotiation.
security.fs.cls.fs_fallback.desc: This older message included legacy fallback material and is not treated as full Forward Secrecy.
security.fs.cls.fs_only.desc: This message is protected by Forward Secrecy only. It cannot be decrypted with the legacy key.
security.fs.cls.strict.desc: This message is protected by Maximum Forward Secrecy. Legacy fallback is disabled.
security.fs.cls.failed.desc: Forward Secrecy decryption failed. The session may have been reset or the device changed.
security.fs.cls.unknown.desc: The security classification of this message could not be determined.
security.pp.section_subtitle: Settings specific to this passphrase-derived identity.
security.pp.timeout_subtitle: Choose a shorter timeout for stronger protection.
security.pp.screen_lock_subtitle: Destroy passphrase keys immediately when the screen locks.
security.warn.active_passphrase: While this identity is unlocked, its keys exist in device memory. Layergram does not protect against seizure or compromise while the identity is actively unlocked.
security.warn.passphrase_fs: The passphrase restores this identity. It may not restore old Forward Secure messages if the required session state was deleted or expired.
security.warn.volatile_history: This mode is designed to reduce future recoverability. Old messages may not be readable again, even with the correct passphrase.
security.warn.ephemeral_session: FS state and history are RAM-only. FS restarts after every passphrase expulsion. No messages or session state will survive.
security.warn.recoverability_body: This mode improves protection by reducing how long old keys or readable history remain available. If you delete messages, reset sessions, expel this identity, reinstall Layergram, lose local state, or clean the encrypted archive, some older messages may not be recoverable even if you still have the original Layergram text or the correct passphrase.
security.warn.recoverability_confirm: I understand that some old messages may become unrecoverable.
security.cleanup.title: Clean undecryptable data
security.cleanup.subtitle: Remove residual data that cannot be decrypted.
security.cleanup.dialog_body: This may permanently delete old encrypted archives, abandoned identity data, passphrase-derived records, security sessions, and other data that Layergram cannot currently decrypt.
security.cleanup.confirm_checkbox: I understand this action is irreversible.
identityQrActionHint: Tap or long-press the QR to share or save it as an image.
identityQrActionsSubtitle: This image contains only your public identity. Use the system sheet to save it to Photos or Files, or send it.
identityQrImageShareFailed: Could not share the QR image
